unit.title: How to select a skirt pattern
unit.needIt: Choosing the right pattern helps you make clothes that fit your unique body shape instead of just fitting a model. It saves you from buying clothes that don't look right or have to be fixed later.
unit.why: A woman wanted a skirt that looked good on her tall frame. She learned that a pattern is just a map of seams. By moving those seams to the right spots, she turned a basic piece of cloth into a perfect fit.
unit.outcome: Adjust a skirt pattern to match your specific body measurements.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when you try on clothes at a store and notice they fit tight in one spot but loose in another. You also see it when you look at a sewing pattern online and wonder if it will actually fit you.
unit.do: Measure your waist and hips today. Fold a tape measure to find the exact half and quarter marks to prepare for your next project.

quiz.q: What should you look for when selecting a skirt pattern?
quiz.why: The text says you should study the lines of the individual to find a style that adds beauty to the figure.
quiz.quote: In selecting a pattern for a skirt the lines of the individual should be studied.

quiz.q: What is the best way to find the half and quarter of your measurements?
quiz.why: The text suggests folding the tape as an easy way to divide the measurements.
quiz.quote: An easy way to do this is to take your waist or hip measurement and then fold the tape, getting just the half, then folding the half and getting the quarter.

quiz.q: What should you do if one side of your body is much larger than the other?
choices: Place a pin at the center front and back
Add more fabric to the side
quiz.why: The text says to place pins at the center front and back to measure and divide correctly.
quiz.quote: If one side is very much larger than the other you can place a pin at the center front and center back and measure from pin to pin

quiz.q: How should you handle a pattern that is too long from the waist to the hip?
choices: Lay a tuck in the pattern
quiz.why: The text says to lay a tuck in the pattern if the distance is too long.
quiz.quote: If the distance from the waist line to the hipe line given on the pattern is too long, lay a tuck in the pattern, making it the required length.

quiz.q: What should you do if the pattern is too short for the desired length?
choices: Cut the pattern and set in paper
quiz.why: The text says to cut the pattern and set in a piece of paper to make it the desired length.
quiz.quote: If the (distance given is not long enough, cut the pattern across and set in a piece of paper, making it the length desired.

quiz.q: How should you handle a skirt that hikes up in front?
choices: Increase the length at the waist line
Add a plait to the front
quiz.why: The text says to increase the length of the pattern in the front at the waist line.
quiz.quote: To remedy this fault it is necessary to increase the length of the pattern in the front at the waist line, adding a little to the sides and tapering off to nothing

quiz.q: What is the rule for a skirt with an uneven number of gores?
choices: Put the odd one in front
quiz.why: The text states that in all gored skirts with an uneven number, the odd one is placed in front.
quiz.quote: In all gored skirts having an uneven number of gores, the odd one is placed in front.

partials: Study the lines of the individual.
Fold the tape to get half and quarter marks.
Adjust the pattern before cutting the cloth.
Use pins to find center points for uneven sides.
Add or subtract inches based on your specific body.
crystal.key: Adjust the paper pattern to match your body measurements before cutting fabric.

decoys.text: Always choose the pattern size that matches your waist.
decoys.why: The text says it is better to choose based on the hip measurement because the waist is easier to alter.

decoys.text: Make all changes to the fabric after it is cut.
decoys.why: The text says to make all alterations in the pattern to avoid wasting material.

crystal.aha: By adjusting the paper pattern first, you ensure the final garment fits perfectly without wasting any fabric.
